T: The cover is not the book. Neither is the menu.
D: Mary Poppins comes back to Cherry Tree Lane to help the grown-up Banks children through hard times.
P: Serve the snacks when Jack and the lamplighters light up the London streets.
S: Crumpets toasted until crisp at the edges, loaded with whipped honey butter that melts into every hole, golden syrup on the side for drizzling. Beat 100g soft butter with 2 tbsp honey and a pinch of flaky salt until pale and fluffy. Toast 8 crumpets under a hot grill or in the toaster for about 3 minutes until crisp on the edges and golden on top. Spread the honey butter on straight away so it sinks into the holes. Stack on a warm plate and serve with a jug of golden syrup.
Cousin Topsy's fix-it shop that turns upside down
Upside-down toasts: bread pressed onto a pan of melted cheddar and fried until a lacy cheese crust forms, flipped and served.
the bathtub that turns into an ocean

Poached prawns on shredded lettuce in small glasses with a cocktail sauce of mayo, tomato sauce and lemon. Peel and devein 600g cooked king prawns, leaving a few tails on for the rims. Mix 120g whole egg mayonnaise with 2 tbsp tomato sauce, 1 tsp Worcestershire, a few drops of Tabasco and the juice of half a lemon. Shred half an iceberg lettuce and divide between 4 glasses. Pile the prawns on top, spoon over the sauce, dust with a pinch of paprika and serve with lemon wedges.
M: Cherry Tree Lane chicken, leek and ham pie
the Banks family home on Cherry Tree Lane

Chicken, leek and ham in a creamy sauce under a puff pastry lid, baked at 200C for 25 minutes, with buttered peas. Brown 800g diced chicken thigh in 30g butter and set aside. Soften 2 sliced leeks in the same pan, stir in 2 tbsp plain flour, then 300ml chicken stock and 150ml cream and simmer until thick. Add the chicken, 150g diced ham and chopped thyme and season. Spoon into a pie dish, cover with 1 sheet puff pastry, cut a slit and brush with beaten egg. Bake at 200C for 25 minutes until golden. Serve with 2 cups peas tossed in butter.
the music hall show inside the painted bowl
Thick pork sausages browned slowly, served on buttery mash with an onion gravy cooked down for 20 minutes, and peas.
W: the balloon lady in the park
Shortcrust rounds filled with strawberry, apricot and blackcurrant jam, baked at 190C for 15 minutes.
K: Fresh lemon juice and sugar syrup shaken with muddled strawberries and mint, topped with soda water and served over ice in tall glasses. Simmer 100g caster sugar with 100ml water until dissolved, then cool. Muddle 250g hulled strawberries with a handful of mint leaves in a jug. Add the syrup and the juice of 5 lemons and stir well. Fill 4 tall glasses with ice, divide the strawberry lemon mix between them and top with 600ml chilled soda water. Garnish with half a strawberry and a mint sprig.

s.how: Scatter grated cheddar in a hot buttered pan and press a slice of white bread on top. Fry until the cheese forms a golden lacy crust, then flip and toast the other side. Cut into fingers and sprinkle with chives. Upside down, of course.

m.note: the music hall show inside the painted bowl
m.how: Brown 8 thick pork sausages slowly in a pan. Cook 2 sliced onions in the same pan until soft, then add 500ml beef stock and simmer 20 minutes until thick. Serve the sausages on mash from 1kg potatoes with peas and plenty of gravy.

w.note: the balloon lady in the park
w.how: Cut shortcrust into rounds and press into a patty tin. Fill a third with strawberry jam, a third with apricot and a third with blackcurrant. Bake at 190C for 15 minutes until the pastry is golden. Dust the edges with icing sugar.
